# Kyoto Spring Trip Plan for Two Adults

A gentle, train-and-bus-friendly 5-day Kyoto itinerary for **2026-04-08 to 2026-04-12** with a **JPY 180,000 total budget** excluding international flights. It balances temples, local food, light hiking, and one traditional bath experience while keeping walking loads manageable for mild knee pain.

## Day-by-Day Kyoto Itinerary

Day 1: Arrival, Gion, and Easy Riverside Evening
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/geo-alt.svg
- Morning: Arrive in Kyoto, drop bags, and take a low-walk start with coffee or tea near Kyoto Station or Gion.
- Afternoon: Visit **Kiyomizu-dera** using bus + short taxi-free approach; keep the pace slow and skip extra hillside detours if knees feel tight.
- Dinner: Try **yudofu** or a set meal in Gion, then a gentle walk along the **Kamo River**.
- Rain backup: Nishiki Market covered stroll + Kyoto Station indoor shopping and food floors.
Media: Image=https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/e/e5/A_store_at_Nishiki_market%2C_Kyoto%2C_Japan.jpg Alt=Rain backup: Nishiki Market covered stroll + Kyoto Station indoor shopping and food floors, Kyoto, Japan
- Lodging area: **Gion/Higashiyama** for a classic first-night base.

Day 2: Arashiyama Temples, Bamboo, and Light Nature
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/tree.svg
- Morning: Go early to **Arashiyama** by train; focus on **Tenryu-ji** and the bamboo grove before crowds build.
- Afternoon: Keep hiking light with the flat river area and optional short visit to **Okochi Sanso** only if energy is good.
- Dinner: Return to central Kyoto for **kaiseki-style lunch/dinner set** or noodles near Kyoto Station.
- Rain backup: **Kyoto Railway Museum** or **Saga-Arashiyama** indoor café and temple stops.
- Lodging area: **Kyoto Station / Central Kyoto** for easier transit and lower walking strain.

Day 3: Northern Temples, Tea, and Bath Time
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/water.svg
- Morning: Visit **Kinkaku-ji** and then **Ryoan-ji** by bus; both are good low-effort temple stops.
- Afternoon: Head to **Nijo Castle** for easier indoor-outdoor sightseeing with plenty of rest points.
- Evening: Book a traditional bath experience at a **sentō** or **onsen-style bath house** with a relaxed soak after sightseeing.
- Dinner: Eat nearby in central Kyoto, aiming for a simple rice bowl, tofu, or soba meal.
- Rain backup: Extend time at **Nijo Castle** and add **Kyoto International Manga Museum**.
- Lodging area: Stay in **Central Kyoto** or keep the same base as Day 2.

Day 4: Fushimi Inari, Sake District, and Local Food
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/signpost-split.svg
- Morning: Visit **Fushimi Inari Taisha** very early; do only the lower torii sections and turn back before the climb becomes tiring.
- Afternoon: Move to **Fushimi** for a sake district walk, tasting, and a slow lunch.
- Dinner: Have **izakaya-style** Kyoto dishes or sushi near your lodging.
- Rain backup: **Fushimi sake museums** and indoor tasting rooms, plus a longer meal break.
- Lodging area: Either remain in **Central Kyoto** or shift to **Fushimi** only if you want a quieter final night.

Day 5: Easy Final Temple Stop and Departure
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/house.svg
- Morning: Choose one gentle final stop such as **To-ji Temple** or a short revisit to a favorite neighborhood for souvenirs.
- Afternoon: Leave time for lunch, packing, and a slow transfer toward Kyoto Station.
- Dinner: Departure meal at Kyoto Station before your evening departure.
- Rain backup: Station-area shopping, food halls, and a final indoor tea stop.
- Lodging area: Keep your final night in **Central Kyoto / Kyoto Station** for the easiest departure.

## Budget Breakdown and Neighborhood Plan

| Item | Estimated Cost | Notes |
|---|---:|---|
| Lodging, 4 nights | JPY 72,000 | Mid-range twin room, 2 neighborhood split if desired |
| Local transport | JPY 12,000 | JR/subway/buses, IC card top-ups, minimal taxis |
| Food and drinks | JPY 42,000 | Mix of casual meals, one nicer dinner, snacks |
| Temple/admission fees | JPY 10,000 | Kiyomizu-dera, Tenryu-ji, Nijo Castle, others |
| Bath experience | JPY 8,000 | Traditional bath or sentō/onsen-style entry + towels |
| Rain backup indoor activities | JPY 8,000 | Museums, café time, market food, extra admissions |
| Buffer for extras | JPY 28,000 | Souvenirs, extra meals, small upgrades |
| Total | **JPY 180,000** | Fits the target budget |

Recommended lodging split:
- **Nights 1–2: Gion/Higashiyama** for atmosphere and temple access
- **Nights 3–4: Central Kyoto / Kyoto Station** for easier transit, less walking, and a smoother departure

## Rain-Day Indoor Swaps for Kyoto

- **Nishiki Market** for covered food sampling and easy pacing
- **Kyoto Railway Museum** for a full indoor half-day
- **Kyoto International Manga Museum** for a relaxed cultural break
- **Nijo Castle** for indoor-heavy sightseeing with manageable walking
- **Tea houses and department-store food halls** near Kyoto Station for low-strain downtime
